## Proof

Let $Y$ follow a Student's $t$-distribution with $\nu$ degrees of freedom (the parameter $\mathcal{w}$ in the problem). We use the convention $\mathrm{VaR}_\beta(Y) = F^{-1}(\beta)$ (the $\beta$-quantile, lower tail) and $\mathrm{ES}_\beta(Y) = \mathbb{E}[Y \mid Y \le \mathrm{VaR}_\beta(Y)] = \frac{1}{\beta}\int_{-\infty}^{\mathrm{VaR}_\beta} y\, f(y)\,dy$. We assume $\nu > 1$ so that the mean (and hence ES) exists.

### Tail behavior of the $t$-distribution

The density is $f(y) = C\,(1+y^2/\nu)^{-(\nu+1)/2}$ with $C = \frac{\Gamma((\nu+1)/2)}{\sqrt{\nu\pi}\,\Gamma(\nu/2)}$. As $x\to\infty$,

$$
1 - F(x) = \int_x^\infty f(t)\,dt \sim C\,\nu^{(\nu+1)/2}\int_x^\infty t^{-(\nu+1)}\,dt = C\,\nu^{(\nu-1)/2}\,x^{-\nu}.
$$

Denote the tail constant $K = C\,\nu^{(\nu-1)/2}$, so $1-F(x)\sim K\,x^{-\nu}$. By symmetry $F(-x)=1-F(x)\sim K\,x^{-\nu}$.

### Asymptotics of $\mathrm{VaR}_\beta$

Set $v = -\mathrm{VaR}_\beta \to +\infty$ as $\beta\to 0^+$. From $\beta = F(-v) \sim K\,v^{-\nu}$ we get

$$
v \sim (K/\beta)^{1/\nu}, \qquad \mathrm{VaR}_\beta \sim -v.
$$

### Asymptotics of $\mathrm{ES}_\beta$

By symmetry $f(-t)=f(t)$, so

$$
\mathrm{ES}_\beta = \frac{1}{\beta}\int_{-\infty}^{-v} y\,f(y)\,dy = -\frac{1}{\beta}\int_v^\infty t\,f(t)\,dt.
$$

For the integral, as $v\to\infty$:

$$
\int_v^\infty t\,f(t)\,dt \sim C\,\nu^{(\nu+1)/2}\int_v^\infty t^{-\nu}\,dt = C\,\nu^{(\nu+1)/2}\,\frac{v^{-(\nu-1)}}{\nu-1} = \frac{K\,\nu}{\nu-1}\,v^{-(\nu-1)}.
$$

Substituting $1/\beta \sim v^\nu/K$:

$$
\mathrm{ES}_\beta \sim -\frac{v^\nu}{K}\cdot\frac{K\,\nu}{\nu-1}\,v^{-(\nu-1)} = -\frac{\nu}{\nu-1}\,v.
$$

### The limit

$$
\frac{\mathrm{VaR}_\beta(Y)}{\mathrm{ES}_\beta(Y)} \sim \frac{-v}{-\frac{\nu}{\nu-1}\,v} = \frac{\nu-1}{\nu}.
$$

Therefore

$$
\boxed{\lim_{\beta\to 0^+}\frac{\mathrm{VaR}_\beta(Y)}{\mathrm{ES}_\beta(Y)} = \frac{\nu-1}{\nu} = 1 - \frac{1}{\nu}.}
$$

This is the standard regularly-varying-tail result: a $t_\nu$ distribution has tail index $\nu$, and for any distribution with tail $\bar F(x)\sim K x^{-\alpha}$ ($\alpha>1$), the extreme-tail ratio $\mathrm{VaR}/\mathrm{ES}\to(\alpha-1)/\alpha$; here $\alpha=\nu$.
